statement: ELIMINATION WITH MERGING: RULE INCOMPLETENESS AND THE GAUSS CONTROL (Fable addendum A3/A6 tested; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Incompleteness: x=0, x=1, y=0, y=1 and the point (2,2) cover F3^2. prune+merge (scratchpad/aelim/merge.py) stops at 5 subspaces, where 1 suffices. The decision itself is correct (decide_m = covered). Rule set recorded as incomplete. The restriction-merge rule (resolution on a linear form) is not added, because a complete procedure decides 3-colourability (Fable Lemma G), so completeness is the decision problem itself. (2) Control (a), dense random linear systems over F3 with k equations in k variables, bad set = 2 hyperplanes per equation (Gauss-solvable): peak subspace count 28 at k=6, 278 at k=8; k=10 did not finish in 300 s. Brute force agrees. So the procedure blows up on instances that Gaussian elimination solves in polynomial time. Its subspace count measures this representation, not the difficulty of the instance. Consistent with Fable Lemma K (cube {0,1}^k, acn = 2^k, from a treewidth-2 instance). Controls (b) and (c) not run: (a) already settles the interpretation. Consequence for the contract (par. 6): counts from 17910/17911 and later G versus Prism(G) comparisons carry no hardness reading. Under fixed orders they compare only representations. The exact open step of this line (Fable A4) is a dag-like lower bound for resolution over linear equations mod 3. That is an open problem in proof complexity, would bound one algorithm family only, and is not an obligation of PNP-001. No obligation closed.

label: 88dcfb6228046559
statement: EXPANSION POINT of the count identity (director's recollection; verify before citing): prod_e p_e(x) has an arithmetic circuit of size O(m) (one product of m small polynomials) - compact and cheap. The whole cost sits in ONE operation: the hypercube sum sum_{x in {0,1}^n}. A hypercube sum of a polynomial-size circuit is exactly Valiant's VNP form; VP vs VNP is open (algebraic analogue of P vs NP; cf. the Chukhin et al. 2026 PIT dichotomy already on file). So for the count identity the question 'where must the compact representation be expanded' has a precise answer - at the hypercube summation - and the open question is which variable-elimination orders keep the partial sums small for which formula structures.

statement: ADDRESSED TABLEAU W(t,i) + ALGEBRAIC EVALUATION UNDER P=NP (owner 2026-11-27; PI analysis; CLAIMED, Claude family; literature from memory). (1) Small circuits for W(t,i) of an EXP machine is the premise EXP subset P/poly (Meyer/Kannan route, PI reply 2026-11-27). Its algebraic version, the low-degree extension of the tableau, is Babai-Fortnow-Lund: EXP subset P/poly => EXP = MA. Under P=NP, MA subset Sigma2 = P, so P=NP => EXP not in P/poly. That is known, and it is no contradiction because the premise is not established (E subset SIZE(2^{o(n)}) contradicts the Impagliazzo-Wigderson hypothesis). (2) Which evaluations ev_S(U_G) does P=NP make polynomial? Boolean (SAT): yes. Tropical with poly-bit weights (min energy, an optimization in P^NP): yes. Approximate counting/marginals (Stockmeyer, in PH): yes. Exact N, Z (#P), F_2 (parity-P), F_p (Mod_pP), C: not known; Toda gives PH subset P^{#P}, the opposite direction. Hence the assumption P=NP does not unlock the exact algebraic evaluations of 17561/17584, so they cannot enter an 'assume P=NP, build a fast algorithm' contradiction as efficient subroutines. No obligation closed.

structure.relationship: S_fanout_001 addresses G0001(ii) by characterizing the exact internal fan-out sequence. The multiplicative composition formula from G0006 (c = log_d(r)) applied to the alternating fan-out [1, 2^n, 1, 2, ...] gives total leaf exponent c = 1 + (log_d 2) * floor((D-1)/2) / n. With MMW19's d = l/(100 s log s), this is c = 1 + O(log s / (n log l)) -> 1 as n grows. This confirms G0007/G0008's conclusion that the per-input-bit reuse exponent a (where r = O(s^a)) does NOT yield c < 1 under MMW19 parameters. The obstacle is not the fan-out magnitude but the fact that layer 2's fan-out of 2^n is exactly the input size, canceling the depth advantage.

structure.text: UNREVIEWED LEMMA (author family claude-haiku, same as this session; needs review by another model family before any use as a premise). STATEMENT: G a graph, c: V->{0,1} with sum_v c(v) even. T(G,c) is the CNF with, for each vertex v, one clause per local edge-assignment at v of parity != c(v); clause width = deg v. Let m = min{deg v : c(v)=1}. CLAIM: every resolution refutation of T(G,c) contains an initial clause of width >= m. PROOF: let x be the all-zero edge assignment. The clause at v forbids a local assignment of parity 0 when c(v)=1, so x falsifies it; x falsifies a clause only if c(v)=1, and then its width is deg v >= m. Suppose every initial clause of a refutation P has width < m. Then x satisfies every initial clause of P. Resolution preserves satisfaction by the fixed assignment x: if x satisfies C or y and D or not-y, then x satisfies C or D (if x(y)=1 it satisfies D, otherwise C). So x satisfies every clause of P, including the empty clause, a contradiction. SCOPE: GF(2) Tseitin CNF only; width only, no size bound. For G=K_n and c = indicator of one vertex, m = n-1. NOT claimed as new: this is a standard one-sided width argument for Tseitin formulas. CONSISTENCY: measured minima K3=2, K4=4, K5>=7 (cm-88c97aad7b8449b6, cm-235f5acd28484ce4) satisfy the bound. It says nothing about the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08, and it closes no named obligation (G0001, G0005 untouched). S0003 and S0004 remain CLAIMED.

statement: THERMODYNAMIC RESPONSE = AFFINE HULL (owner 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family). Z_G(beta,h) = sum_sigma exp(-beta H_G(sigma) + <h, X(sigma)>), X in {0,1}^{3n} one-hot. grad_h^2 log Z = Cov(X) under the Gibbs measure (exponential family). At h=0 and beta -> infinity the measure tends to the uniform one on proper 3-colourings (G 3-colourable; finite sum, continuity), so the limit Hessian is C_G = Cov_unif(X). Since a^T C_G a = Var(a^T X), ker C_G = {a : a^T X constant on colourings}, and rank C_G = dim aff{X(sigma)} = 2 dim W_G by 17497 (the direction space is W_G (x) U). STRENGTH: a correct identity and an equivalent restatement of 17497 (the covariance of a uniform measure has rank equal to the dimension of the affine hull of its support). Evaluating C_G is as hard as the hull (17497 (2)).

statement: PB VIEW OF THE BLIND CASES (corrected): if every variable occurs in a clause, a NONNEGATIVE integer solution of A x = 1 is automatically 0/1 (x_i + x_j + x_k = 1 with x >= 0 integer forces each term <= 1). So positive 1-in-3-SAT is exactly 'does A x = 1 have a nonnegative integer solution' - the upper bounds x <= 1 are redundant and the information GF(3) misses splits into (i) integrality (30 of the 1,350 blind sets at n=6 have no integer solution; depth-1 CG from A x = 1 refutes exactly these, D-023) and (ii) SIGN (the other 1,320 have integer solutions, all with negative entries). The LP over x >= 0 is always feasible (x = 1/3, D-016h). Owner's worked example (clauses 012,013,023,045,124, n=6, GF(3)-blind): integer solutions exist, e.g. (1,0,0,0,1,-1) and (-1,1,1,1,-1,3) in [-3,3]^6, none nonnegative; refuted by clause differences, x_0 >= 0 and ONE rounding step (2t <= 1 => t <= 0) - a rank-1 cutting-plane proof using only nonnegativity.

statement: NORMALIZATION: SCOPE OF REVERSIBILITY AND THE THREE PROPERTIES (owner 2026-11-27; PI derivation; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Exact for the block constructions. The t-copy family (t copies per vertex, y_1 = ... = y_t, edges between all copy pairs; primal graph G[K_t], tw = t(tw(G)+1) - 1) preserves U_G by the monomial substitution X_{v,c} -> prod_i X_{v,i,c}. Hybrid elimination (17919) removes the linear block equations by substitution in polynomial time and returns G. The prism pipeline Prism(G) -> affine normal form -> block encoding -> coordinate change -> G is exact and polynomial (17921-17923). w_sem = tw(G)+1 throughout (17924). B(b,t) = t b and its mixed difference 1 are arithmetic of a bilinear formula with no complexity content. (2) Owner restriction: 'every semantics-preserving structural growth can be reversed efficiently' is NOT proved in general. It is proved only for these block constructions. (3) Three properties to keep apart: (a) semantic equivalence of two representations (same solution set or same U_G up to substitution); (b) existence of a normal form; (c) efficient computability of it. The prism construction has all three. (4) PI statement for general representations (folklore-level, no citation): let c map constraint representations to representations such that c(phi) = c(psi) iff phi and psi have the same solution set. A polynomial-time canonical form c exists iff P = NP. If c is polynomial-time, then phi is unsatisfiable iff c(phi) = c(false), so the coNP-complete problem UNSAT is in P. Conversely, under P = NP take c(phi) = the lexicographically first representation of size <= |phi| equivalent to phi. It is found by prefix search over a Sigma_2 predicate and is polynomial-time because PH = P. So efficient canonical normalization of general representations is another equivalent form of the hypothesis (family of 17920, Proposition E), and it relativizes. Existence (b) holds trivially by this definition; the content lies in (c) and in restricting the admissible operations. (5) Open question, precisely stated: for a fixed admissible class N (block-local bijections, linear substitution, existential elimination of locally determined variables), which structural invariants of a representation survive every composition of operations from N? Candidate: w_sem of the nonlinear residual. Its invariance under N is not proved. A positive answer measures what the mathematics represents, not decision complexity. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: reversibility exact for block constructions only; efficient canonical normal form for general representations iff P=NP

statement: RETRACTION of one sentence of 17554 + owner theorem (2026-11-27; PI check fg_cov_check.py; CLAIMED, Claude family). RETRACTED: 'computing C_G is as hard as the hull' (only 'at least as hard' holds). THEOREM (owner): (A) G bipartite implies W_G = Q^n (colour one side 1, the other from {2,3}; each vertex of the second side is its own (2,3)-component, so b_K = +-e_v; swap the roles of the sides), hence dim aff = 2n. (B) For any H on n vertices, B_k(H) (each edge replaced by k = 2n+1 internally disjoint length-2 paths) is bipartite with P_{B_k(H)}(3) = sum_j rho_H(j) 2^{kj}, so P_H(3) = P_{B_k(H)}(3) mod 2^k. statement: RANK THRESHOLDS UNDER P = NP AND EXPORT REFRESH FOR FABLE (owner 2026-11-27; PI check). (1) Owner precision, checked. P = NP forces no polynomial rank bound, but it makes polynomially bounded rank thresholds efficiently checkable. rank(M) >= k iff some k x k submatrix is nonsingular. For an implicitly given matrix (exponentially many rows and columns, entries computable in polynomial time) and k <= poly, that is an NP predicate (guess indices, compute the determinant), so it is decidable under P = NP. For an explicitly given M, rank is in P unconditionally (Gaussian elimination), so the statement has content only for implicit matrices such as compatibility matrices indexed by colourings. Like 17920 it uses only 'NP predicate, hence decidable' and therefore relativizes. It yields no contradiction. Addendum B (Fable: padding lemma + compatibility rank) is to be recorded as negative knowledge per 17926; its text is still not in PI files. (2) Process measure: so that Fable reviews the accumulated knowledge, the research-graph export was rebuilt with the unchanged builder (scratchpad/exporttool/export/build_export.py). Source: MMW19 (STOC 2019, abstract verified via web_read of people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf): 'If search-MCSP[n^c] lacks Õ(N)-size, Õ(1)-depth circuits for a c >= 1, then NP not in P/poly.' Consequence: the earlier H2 (a size transfer from NP in P/poly to small MCSP circuits) is not a separate premise; the cited theorem performs that transfer. Bare-chain objection applies only to a lower bound without the stated size/depth class. H1 (for every fixed k, CC(MCSP[m^c]) > N(log N)^k infinitely often, general circuits) lacks Õ(N)-size circuits of any depth, so it implies the MMW hypothesis for c fixed. OPEN: (a) the exact theorem text (hypotheses and 'lacks' = for all or infinitely many input lengths); (b) the decision-to-search step: H1 for decision CC implies search lack, since a search-MCSP circuit for size m^c can be checked against the table in N·polylog time; (c) the quantifier. Not a P != NP claim. The arithmetic table cm-908028e6543b4a10 is exploratory and does not bear on H2.

statement: SOURCE CHECK, MMW19 Thm 1.4 (verbatim from the people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf chunk at offset 13500, jina-reader extraction; sha256 7077714ba22dead7). Let s(n) >= n and A in PH. (i) If there is eps>0 such that for all c>=1, search-MCSP^A[2^{eps n/c}] on inputs of length N=2^n does not have N^{1+eps}-size O(1/eps)-depth TC0 circuits, then NP not in TC0. (ii) If search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on N=2^n does not have circuits of N*poly(s(n)) size and O(log N) depth, then NP not in NC1. (iii) If search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on N=2^n does not have circuits of N*poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP not in P/poly. Status: this is the TEXT as extracted (the exponent form 2^{eps n/c} is read from the extraction, not from a second source). This is a source check only; it does not settle whether the K1 target falls under Thm 1.4 (that needs the Thm 1.7 row D and the exact K1 parameters).

statement: Correction to the APPROACH record 05c3fbb2815cdff5 (ANSWERED). Only the H2 sub-point of K11-D5 is closed: the NP-in-P/poly-to-small-MCSP-circuits conversion is inside MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (A in PH, s(n) >= n; primary PDF offset 13500, proof offset 53500). Still open: (i) the quantifier 'infinitely many n' is an inference from the contrapositive proof, not verbatim text; (ii) the decision-to-search transfer (flag bit of a search circuit is a decision circuit of the same size and depth) is argued, not checked against the exact search-MCSP output format; (iii) H1, a general-circuit lower bound N*(log N)^k for decision MCSP[m^c] for every fixed k, infinitely often, is unproved. The source itself (offset 13500) states that proving even lower bounds for O(N)-size O(log N)-depth circuits 'remains an open challenge in complexity theory', so H1 is a strong superlinear general-circuit bound for a function in NP, not a near-term target. The dispute K11-D5 is therefore narrowed, not resolved; the decision should read CONTINUE for the H1 obligation or ESCALATE to the magnification tree (Q-10bbdfaf2a, Q-f1e058b72f).

statement: ALGORITHM-STRUCTURE DIRECTION MAPPED TO EXISTING RESULTS (owner proposal 2026-11-27: apply the universal function to a hypothetical polynomial-time solver instead of the solution set; PI graph check before derivation). (1) Already in the graph. T43 Lemma B (2026-11-18): every fan-in-2 circuit C of size s has a parsimonious positive 1-in-3 encoding phi_C (read <= 3, O(s) variables, input set X, exactly one extension per accepting input), built in time poly(s). This is the owner's 'algorithm graph H_n'. T43 sec. 4: the uniform bridge P != NP would need is a P-uniform, scaled-down algorithmic method (nontrivial SAT algorithm against P-uniform circuits plus diagonalization inside NP); not known. 17143: exclusion criterion 'black-box bound with no white-box transfer'. 17359: P != NP is uniform, natural proofs concern circuit lower bounds, relativization and algebrization concern every uniform route. (2) What the construction forces (PI). Under P = NP, a P-uniform circuit family C_n computes the selection S (Fable Prop E). H_n = phi_{C_n} gives U_{H_n}(X,Y) = sum over inputs x of X^x Y^{comp(x)}: one monomial per input. The only relation forced between U_G and U_{H_n} is correctness: the output part of the monomial for input G is a monomial of U_G, or the UNSAT symbol iff U_G = 0. The internal gates are unconstrained beyond correctness and uniformity. Any further forced property of the gates is a P-uniform circuit lower bound for S, which is equivalent to P != NP (T45 Lemma T5). (3) Barrier placement. White-box use of the gates avoids relativization only if a step uses the gate structure. An algebraic analysis of U_{H_n} (arithmetization of the computation) is the setting of Aaronson-Wigderson algebrization (cited from memory, verify at source): such steps algebrize unless they use more than low-degree extensions. A property derived from truth tables of the circuits must avoid the natural-proofs conditions (largeness, constructivity). (4) Unused joint consequence (candidate, owner to decide): T43 Q-BD asks whether satisfiability of Lemma-B images phi_C with functional backdoor X (|X| = n) is decidable in 2^n / n^{omega(1)} poly(|phi|). The hybrid elimination of 17919/17921 is exactly a tool for that structure: clauses are linear equations mod 3, the rest is forced by the backdoor. A saving gives NEXP not in P/poly via Williams (not P != NP; T43). This is a concrete point where the new mathematics meets an existing bridge without a lower-bound premise. No obligation closed.

structure.text: CORRECTION to edc7f308163e419c (UNREVIEWED; author family claude-haiku = this session, needs review by another model family before any use as a premise). The lemma's hypothesis must read sum_v c(v) ODD, not even: each edge contributes to two vertex parities, so the Tseitin formula is satisfiable when the total charge is even, and the K_n application (one odd vertex) requires odd. Statement, corrected: G graph, c: V->{0,1} with sum_v c(v) odd; T(G,c) = CNF with, for each vertex v, one clause per local edge-assignment at v of parity != c(v) (clause width deg v); m = min{deg v : c(v)=1}. Every resolution refutation of T(G,c) contains an initial clause of width >= m. Proof unchanged (all-zero assignment x falsifies the clause at v iff c(v)=1; resolution preserves satisfaction by a fixed x; so x satisfies the empty clause if all initial clauses have width < m). For G=K_n with one odd vertex, m = n-1. SCOPE: GF(2) Tseitin only; width only, no size bound; says nothing about the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08. NOT claimed as new (standard one-sided width argument for Tseitin). Closes no named obligation (G0001, G0005 untouched).

bingo.correctness: [x satisfies F] = prod over clauses C of (1 - [x falsifies C]); expand the product and sum over x in {0,1}^n. A product of falsification indicators over S is 1 exactly on assignments falsifying every clause of S, which exist iff S is consistent, and then fix |V(S)| variables. Verified by cm-b4aa92c386b14b14 (400 random CNFs, 0 mismatches; VERIFICATION, own code).
bingo.effect: #F = sum over S subset of clauses of (-1)^|S| * 2^(n-|V(S)|) * [S consistent]; S consistent iff no variable is forced to both values by the literals of S

bingo.limitations: 2^m terms, exponential in m; a counting identity, not a polynomial algorithm; yields no lower bound by itself

statement: BIT-COST RULE for every algorithmic claim in PNP-001 (owner 2026-11-19, physical vs abstract model): costs are counted in bits on the classical model. Operations on numbers whose size grows with n (exact counts Z(F) = sum_x prod_e p_e(x), polynomial coefficients, determinants, rational solutions, tensor entries) are charged by their bit length; a method that is polynomial only under unit-cost arithmetic is not a polynomial algorithm (unit-cost multiplication RAM = PSPACE). A faster physical or alternative model counts for P = NP only if it is classically simulable with polynomial overhead.

Barriers (relativization, natural proofs, algebrization) rule out technique classes, they are not conditions every proof must satisfy.

statement: REFINEMENT of 17548: first formal step pinned (PI source reading, commit 3344da5). In proof order, the hypothesis first enters through fixed_templates_of_small_circuits -> wire_expanders_of_small_circuits -> cube_obstruction (l >= 18C^2: small circuits for P n exclude the Euclidean cube from every spectral wire metric) -> not_small_universal_of_exact_tensorPower_layout / sharp_tensor_layout (every tensor's powers are projections of P_M: TensorPowerCNF.sharp_projection) -> BalancedPowerObstruction -> Circuit.spectralValue_le_balanced_cost -> Circuit.exists_balanced_cutFactors. That lemma is the first formal operation: from c.exists_parseGrammar and homogeneousComponent, every party-selecting coefficient equals sum_S M_S over balanced cuts (|I| <= 3|S| <= 2|I|) with rank M_S <= |I|(|I||J| + s + 1). It uses the degree grading of a formal circuit. Everything after it (spectral values, layouts, cube geometry) uses only these cut factors. BOOLEAN ANALOGUE fails at exactly this lemma: (owner theorem, PI check) the AC0 predicate 'A is a permutation matrix with a_{11} = 1, B has exactly one 1 per row, and not a_{k,i} or not a_{k+1,j} or b_{ij} cyclically' has exactly one accepted (A, B) per directed Hamiltonian cycle. Its generating polynomial projects (X = 1, Y_{ij,0} = 1, Y_{ij,1} = z_{ij}) onto HC_N. Classically (Valiant 1979, from memory) the permutation-matrix predicate alone gives the permanent. Hence 'small Boolean predicate => small formal generating polynomial' for AC0 would put HC and perm in VP, i.e. VP = VNP. This is unconditional and does not use OpenAI; with OpenAI's claimed bound it would be false. The analogue of exists_balanced_cutFactors for Boolean circuits is therefore not a lemma that can be proved without settling VP vs VNP. STRENGTH: locates the non-transferable step; no Boolean lower bound; no obligation closed.

statement: POTTS DEGREE-2 DECOMPOSITION (owner 2026-11-27 local sums; PI global identity, potts_check.py: 200 random graphs, exact polynomial equality; CLAIMED, Claude family). H_G(sigma) = #monochromatic edges, Z_G(x) = sum over 3-colourings of x^{H_G}, x = e^{-1/T}; rho_G(k) are its coefficients; F(G) in SAT iff rho_G(0) > 0. For p of degree 2 with neighbours u, v: local sums 2 + x^2 (sigma(u) = sigma(v)) and 1 + 2x (otherwise). Hence Z_G(x) = (1+2x) Z_{G-p}(x) + (1-x)^2 Z_{(G-p)/uv}(x), with contraction as a multigraph (parallel edges kept, a loop from uv in E contributes x). At x=0: P_G(3) = P_{G-p}(3) + P_{(G-p)/uv}(3), and e_p in W_G (17507) iff P_{(G-p)/uv}(3) > 0. STRENGTH: an exact identity and an equivalent restatement of 17507; no lower bound. Landscape quantities (gap, ruggedness, entropy, OGP) bound only restricted algorithm classes (local or stable or low-degree), and zero-free regions give algorithms (Barvinok, Patel-Regts; from memory, verify); none quantifies over all algorithms.

statement: The edge-variable formula Phi(G) is exactly a perfect-matching encoding: its satisfying assignments correspond bijectively to perfect matchings of G. Thus the cubic-graph restriction translates positive 1-in-3 satisfiability into general-graph perfect matching, a polynomial-time problem; this is a structural reduction and makes no progress toward P != NP.

label: 9fc74350aab930ea
statement:
T50 (theory/T50-external-vpvnp-mechanism-and-boolean-transfer-2026-11-27.md): mechanism analysis of UNVERIFIED external VP!=VNP proofs (OpenAI Nov 23, Anthropic). Kept separate from established results; only the overviews have been read; Lean verification is pending. Owner decision recorded: T48 is consolidated, Q-BD is closed as a route, and the global contradiction mechanism is the focus.
Mechanism (both papers): a win-win dichotomy on a geometric hypothesis about tensor prices (spectral points/wire lengths). Flat case: rigidity, i.e. small rank across balanced cuts, gives a direct bound. Contracting case: wire saving lets a hypothetical small circuit be replayed faster, giving an accelerator (v^H steps in v^{H-16}) that iterates; a diagonal argument shows there are none (thm_noacc). The circuit enters only in two steps (arrows C: lem_balanced, lem_lowdeg), which use the block-multilinear and low-degree parts of the gate polynomials.
Boolean break point (B1): Boolean correctness lives in F[x]/I, which is only filtered, not graded (x^2 -> x). A Boolean circuit computes g = f + sum (x_i^2-x_i)h_i (Anthropic sec.2.5; = T49 Lemma3, T48 sec.3). The graded parts of g are not those of f; the explicit h_i (T48 8.1/9.1) do not help.
Required bridge MT (multilinearization transfer): a Boolean circuit of size s for multilinear f over F2 gives an arithmetic circuit of size poly(s) for f. NF(g) is always in VNP_2. (B2) MT plus the external theorem would only give parity-P not in P/poly (HC over F2 = parity of #HC; Valiant criterion, from memory), and P=NP is not known to imply parity-P in P/poly. Counting vs existence: no tool is known. (B3) The Boolean analogue of the accelerator diagonal needs a fixed exponent saving; P=NP gives only NTIME(t) in DTIME(t^c) with c>=1. The known Boolean speedup/slowdown contradictions are alternation trading (T27, closed).
First unproved implication on this route: MT. Together with the external theorem it is itself a Boolean lower bound, so it is not a small step, and it would still be parity-P, not NP. Next steps: Lean builds plus #print axioms, then the appendices (lem_balanced, lem_lowdeg, thm_noacc).

structure.conclusion: External VP!=VNP mechanism = geometric dichotomy (rigidity vs accelerator+diagonal); Boolean transfer breaks at grading (F[x]/I ungraded); bridge MT needed, would reach only parity-P; contracting-case Boolean analogue = closed T27

statement: For any length-N language L, a layered prefix machine can maintain the literal prefix using O(N)-size transitions independent of L; the hard part for succinct L is endpoint membership. For L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), endpoint membership is the corresponding circuit-size-threshold decision on the complete truth table, so cheap prefix updates alone do not supply an efficient MCSP recognizer.

statement: Correction to my previous CONNECTION record (S-a711679438). The decision-to-search step (b) was argued by checking a search circuit's output against the table; that argument is not needed. Direction needed: a search-MCSP solver of size Õ(N) and depth Õ(1) has a flag output bit (1 iff some circuit of size <= s exists). That bit is a decision circuit with the same size and depth. So a lower bound 'no decision circuit of size N(log N)^k for any depth' implies 'search-MCSP[m^c] lacks Õ(N)-size, Õ(1)-depth circuits' for the fixed k. This is EXPLORATION-level reasoning, not a verified lemma. Still open: (a) whether MMW's 'lacks' means for all sufficiently large n or infinitely many n, (b) whether MMW's oracle A can be the empty oracle (A in PH is trivially allowed), (c) the exact search output convention in MMW. H1 remains a conditional hypothesis, not a known result; nothing here claims P != NP.

label: 457a96b4e2326f51
statement: OWNER DECISION ON THE GROWTH PARAMETER AND THE PADDING LEMMA (owner 2026-11-27; NEGATIVE KNOWLEDGE; PI partial check). Source status: Fable's 'Addendum B' (padding lemma) and the owner's 'compatibility rank' are not in the PI files; their exact statements are not checked by the PI. Decision (owner): the structural growth parameter t is excluded as an independent proof route. Padding is recorded as negative knowledge. No return to the alternation route T27. U_G stays the primary object. PI-checkable part, t-copy padding of 17925: U_{G(t)}(X) = U_G evaluated at X_{v,c} = prod_{i<=t} X_{v,i,c}. For 3-colourable G it is homogeneous of degree t n (one variable per vertex copy); otherwise U_G = 0 and every padding is the zero polynomial. Circuit size grows at most additively by O(t n) multiplication gates for the substitution, so cost is not fully neutral. The growth is explained entirely by the explicit recoding, and the converse projection X_{v,i,c} = 1 for i >= 2 recovers U_G. Owner restriction, accepted: it is not proved that only time exponents and alternation depth are complexity-relevant parameters. Principle: treewidth, number of variables, polynomial degree and formal state space can all be changed by explicit recodings without changing the solution information (17921-17925). This explains why these structure measures do not capture general computational hardness. Semantic invariants (w_sem, and the compatibility rank per the owner) do not consume the hypothesis P = NP either. Next question (owner): which intrinsic properties of U_G would P = NP change or force? No obligation closed.

statement: DIRECTOR SYNTHESIS (classical facts (director's recollection of classical results; verify before citing)): the Tutte-barrier family on which the measured local GF(3) Nullstellensatz degree reached 4 (k=17) encodes PERFECT MATCHING, which is in P (Edmonds 1965). Edmonds' matching polytope = degree equations + odd-set inequalities, and odd-set inequalities are rank-1 Chvatal-Gomory cuts (sum the degree equations of an odd component, divide by 2, round). So cutting planes should refute these formulas with short proofs, exactly like the pigeonhole example: our NS-degree data on this family measure a LIMIT OF NULLSTELLENSATZ, not hardness of the problem. Test: short cutting-plane refutations of the k=5..17 instances.

label: c4cd137f2191cda4
statement: GRAPH-NATIVE TRANSFER OF THE CUT-FACTOR STEP FAILS FOR BOOLEAN COMPUTATION (PI 2026-11-27; CLAIMED, Claude family; standard fact). Graph: n disjoint 2-paths a_i-b_i-c_i; edge variables x_i={a_i,b_i}, y_i={b_i,c_i}. f(G) = parity of the number of i with both edges present (= inner product IP_n). Boolean circuit size O(n) (n AND + n-1 XOR). For the balanced edge cut {x} | {y}, the communication matrix has rank 2^n - 1 (0/1) and 2^n (+-1), checked numerically for n=2..8 (scratch ip_rank.py). Hence 'small computation on graph G implies low rank across balanced edge cuts' is false for Boolean gates. The OpenAI step exists_balanced_cutFactors needs homogeneous degree and parse grammar (sums of products), not graph structure. Consequence: a graph-native version of the geometric contradiction must either restrict to monotone/positive operations (then it is the arithmetic case of 17561, and Razborov's monotone bound for perfect matching, from memory, shows such bounds also hold for problems in P) or use a graph invariant that is NOT bounded by cut rank. No obligation closed.

structure.barrier_diagnostic: Relativizing: the collision argument is language-agnostic given exact correctness, so likely relativizing within this model. Natural: not established; the affine state bound is not a constructive combinatorial property yielding a learner. Algebrizing: unresolved in the standard sense; field-linear states alone do not settle oracle extensions. Localizing: applies to fixed affine transitions; robustness to small fan-in oracle gates is untested.
structure.circumvention_tests: Reversible computing: no universal cost claim, only a bound for fixed affine state maps. Strassen/cancellation: cancellation is accounted for by the group-algebra coefficient argument. Barrington: outside this model; width-5 branching programs remain outside scope. Catalytic space: borrowed/restored auxiliary state is not modeled. Mass production: no claim about copies or amortization.
structure.connection: The additive group of F_{p^r}^S is an elementary abelian p-group of rank rS, so the group-algebra argument transfers with augmentation-ideal nilpotence degree rS(p-1)+1.

CONSEQUENCE for G0001(ii): the oracle gates read each input bit at most O~(s) times per replacement, so r <= O~(s) from those gates alone. statement: STATE-SUM INTEGRATION (owner 2026-11-27). SOURCE: 'Paths, trees and grids separate Valiant's hierarchy', OpenAI manuscript in the public repo openai/math, dated 2026-11-24, not peer-reviewed; per the repo's Lean doc the separations are Lean-checked for degree-component border circuits, and the explicit n^{Omega((log n)^{1/12})} grid bound is not formalised. Definition (paper eq. 1.1): Z_{G,q}(X) = sum_{a in [q]^E} prod_v X_{v, a|E(v)}, with an independent table at each vertex. IDENTITY (PI proof, statesum_check.py: path q=3, triangle, multi-edge, C4 equal as monomial multisets): Phi_{G,q} on positive exact-one clauses: per edge EO(y_{e,1..q}); per vertex EO(s_{v,alpha} : alpha in [q]^{E(v)}); for e in E(v), i in [q]: EO({y_{e,j}: j != i} u {s_{v,alpha}: alpha_e = i}), equivalent to y_{e,i} = sum_{alpha_e = i} s_{v,alpha}. The solutions are in bijection with a in [q]^E. Long clauses go to 3-ary positive exact-one parsimoniously: EO(x1,x2,z), EO(z,z',F), EO(z',x3,...), with z, z' determined and F the constant 0 from the T41 gadget E(T,a,b), E(T,b,c), E(T,c,a) (unique solution T=1, a=b=c=0). With weight X_{v,alpha} on s_{v,alpha} and 1 on every other variable, P_Phi(X) = sum_{y in Sol(Phi)} prod_{s_{v,alpha}=1} X_{v,alpha} = Z_{G,q}(X). So Z is a projection of the generic generating polynomial of an Exact-One family, and any arithmetic lower bound for Z transfers to it. ARITHMETIC vs BOOLEAN: the transfer stops at arithmetic circuits computing the polynomial formally. COUNTEREXAMPLE to any 'arithmetic generating-polynomial bound => Boolean decision bound' rule: bipartite perfect matching is decidable in P, yet its generating polynomial is the permanent (VNP-complete; the companion manuscript claims superpolynomial bounds for it). Known implications run the other way (Buergisser: NP not in P/poly plus GRH => VP != VNP over C, from memory, verify). No Boolean lower bound, no closure of OBL-R2/R6/R7/R8/ST-ABS/Q-C, and no P != NP progress follows, even if the manuscript is correct.

statement: Correction to 17428 (owner 2026-11-27). (i) The zero gadget E(x,y,z), E(x,y,w), E(z,w,r) forces z=w=0 but leaves two extensions (x,y) in {(1,0),(0,1)}: not parsimonious. Parsimonious chains use the T41 constant gadget E(T,a,b), E(T,b,c), E(T,c,a) (unique: T=1, a=b=c=0). The degree statement of 17428 (projection = graph of AND_n, min max degree n) is unaffected. (ii) ECCC TR22-038 (Impagliazzo-Mouli-Pitassi) carries a correction of 2026-02-25 (owner's check): the extension-variable lower bound currently holds only for extension variables depending on disjoint sets of original variables; overlapping carry constructions are not covered, so it does not touch the width-vs-size gap of 17409.

K_{m,s} is fixed by (m,s); clause 3 only needs some spanning family B_A of K with small overlap treewidth, not a linear model of A's state transitions. The repository states Lean formalizations of VF<VBP<VP<VNP over every field (lean/ComparatorChallenges/VPVNP.lean, ArithmeticHierarchy.lean); not built or checked here. STATUS: published claims, not independently verified; usable only with that label. (i) has no Boolean analogue through the arithmetised degree (seq 17269, 17275: every representation has degree Omega(r^2 q^4)); a Boolean use needs a decomposition of Boolean circuits into few pieces, each 'simple across some balanced slot cut', and no such theorem for general Boolean circuits is known to the director (known Boolean analogues are restricted models with best-partition communication bounds). This is recorded as the precise missing piece, not as a new obligation or lane.

statement: INTERFERENCE = GF(3) CHARACTER SUMS (director synthesis for the spatiotemporal handover): a clause test x_i + x_j + x_k = 1 (mod 3) written with phases is (1/3) sum_t omega^{t(x_i+x_j+x_k-1)}, omega = e^{2 pi i/3}. Summed over the whole group F_3^n, the interference total is 3^(n-r) or 0 - exactly GF(3) consistency, computable by linear algebra, and blind to the 1,350 sets at n=6. Restricted to the Boolean cube {0,1}^n the same phases give the exact count Z(F) - a hypercube sum (VNP form), with no group structure to exploit. So a linear wave/interference model reproduces our known dichotomy: the efficient part is GF(3), the exact part is the hypercube sum. Readout: SAT formulas with exactly one solution exist (C = 1 rows in topic_onein3), so a normalised Boolean amplitude can be 2^-n. The QUBO energy E_F(x) = sum (x_i+x_j+x_k-1)^2 is an integer, so its SAT/UNSAT gap is always >= 1 (good readout margin) - the cost then sits in reaching the minimum, i.e. in the dynamics.

structure.text: Gap G0001 input: CJSW arXiv 2203.14379 Theorem 1.3 (web_read offset 16500, sha256 c09885f6e64c6c99d9043a5dccc59422752b1ceabf7102cea48d82c842d7d568). Verbatim: 'Let f(n) >= omega(1). For every language L in NP, a P^NP-constructive separation of L from uniform randomized streaming algorithms with O(n (log n)^{f(n)}) time and O((log n)^{f(n)}) space implies EXP^NP != BPP.' So the exponent is f(n) = omega(1) (an unbounded function), not a fixed constant. The model is randomized and uniform, with a P^NP refuter. It is NOT deterministic one-pass search-MCSP with update time, so it does not directly give the K1 target. Lemma 3.2 and the hypothesis check for K1 remain unread. Outcome: exponent gap partly resolved; the deterministic one-pass transfer is still open. Not progress toward P vs NP.

statement: CORRECTION to Q-f0a0962f12 turn 3: the structural finding is not a conditional bound. Clauses 1-4 of Candidate A are jointly unsatisfiable (LB <= tw(H_B) <= F < LB), using Thm 4.1 and subgraph-monotonicity of tw. The earlier 'conditional lower bound, not a contradiction' wording was wrong. Clause 5 remains OPEN. Clause 2/3 'REFUTED as stated' was also too strong: there is no counterexample, only an undefined map A -> B_A for nonlinear algorithms. Chen-Jin-Santhanam-Williams, 'Constructive Separations and Their Consequences', arXiv 2203.14379, Theorem 1.7 (read verbatim from the web_read result at offset 22000, jina-reader extraction, paper p.9/41). Let s(n) >= n log(n)^{omega(1)} be time-constructive super-quasipolynomial; MCSP[s(n)] and Parity at input length N = 2^n. (1) If there exists a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm, then P != NP. (2) If PH not in SIZE(s(n)^2), there is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. (3) For s(n) <= o(2^n/n), there is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[2^poly(s(n))] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. (4) There is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] list-refuter for Parity against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. Scope: the model is AC0 refuters against AC0 algorithms (constructive separations). It is NOT a general-circuit lower bound for Gap-MCSP at the row-A threshold and does not feed the K1 target (general circuits, deterministic one-pass search-MCSP). statement: CHROMATIC POLYNOMIAL (owner 2026-11-27; PI check). Whitney: P_G(q) = sum_{A subset E} (-1)^{|A|} q^{c(V,A)}. F(G) satisfiable iff P_G(3) > 0 (number of proper 3-colourings). Degree-2 membership (17507): e_p in W_G iff some colouring has col(u) = col(v); for uv not an edge, deletion-contraction gives P_{G+uv}(3) = P_G(3) - P_{G/uv}(3), and P_{G/uv}(3) counts exactly the colourings with col(u) = col(v); so e_p in W_G iff P_{G+uv}(3) < P_G(3) (if uv is an edge, both sides are false). Correct. KNOWN CANCELLATION THEORY: for the Tutte plane (P_G(q) is a Tutte evaluation at (1-q, 0)), Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh 1990 (from memory, verify) prove #P-hardness except on the hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = 1 and a few special points, where the Whitney sum collapses (e.g. matrix-tree, a determinant). q = 3 gives (-2, 0), (x-1)(y-1) = 3, hard. So exponential term count is not cost, and the efficient cancellations of this family are classified, but only relative to #P-hardness. An unconditional cancellation-impossibility theorem for P_G(3) is a Boolean lower bound (P_G(3) as a function of the graph's bits), and the multivariate Potts generating polynomial in edge weights is the arithmetic object of 17540, where arithmetic hardness does not transfer.

statement: RECURSIVE COMPOSITION + MinGraph CANNOT YIELD A CONTRADICTION (PI 2026-11-27; CLAIMED, Claude family). Owner transfer: R_{j+1}(a,b) <-> exists c R_j(a,c) & R_j(c,b), G_{j+1} = MinGraph(G_j o G_j); under P=NP the run time is poly(s, K_max, log T). Correct as stated. (1) Strength of the premise: K_max = poly(s) for all transition maps with s-bit state means every DSPACE(s) computation has a poly(s)-size EXISTENTIAL graph representation, i.e. PSPACE inside NP/poly. Unproven and believed false. With only exists-quantifiers the size doubles per level; the Savitch/TQBF reuse of one copy needs a forall per level, i.e. log T = poly alternations, outside every fixed level of PH, so P=NP does not collapse it. (2) Even with the premise the conclusion is P=PSPACE: DTIME(t) in DSPACE(t) in DTIME(t^d) contradicts no hierarchy theorem. Relative to A = TQBF we have P^A = NP^A = PSPACE^A, and all steps relativize, so no contradiction is possible. EXP would need exponential state s, so K_max >= s is exponential. (3) The affine case M^{2^k} by repeated squaring is correct but trivial (the affine class is closed under composition). No obligation closed.

statement: T41-D6 JOINT SCHUR (owner 2026-11-27), CLAIMED, author-checked (Claude family): schur_t41_check.py, 400 random read<=3 positive 1-in-3 instances, 2644 principal minors, parity over F_2 and weighted over GF(2^19). (a) W subset V\T maximal nonsingular principal block of B[V\T] (principal rank property, symmetric): det B[V\U] = det C * det K[Wbar\U] for all U subset T; K[R,R]=0 with |R| = nu = dim ker B[V\T]; nu > |T\U| kills the term; nu > |T| => #SAT even. (b) Weighted B(X) (one weight per 1-2-occurrence variable, char 2): det B(X)[V\U(S)] != 0 <=> residual instance satisfiable (cycles >=3 cancel in reverse pairs, covers give distinct monomials); nu(X) > |T| => unsatisfiable; kernel |T|+nu <= 2|T|; randomized poly preprocessing over GF(2^{|H|+O(log m)}). Strength: (a) is the principal pivot transform; nu > |T| is a deficiency/pigeonhole certificate (each uncoverable clause of V\T needs its own T clause), never triggered in the sample; cost of the remaining sum unchanged, poly*2^|H|, and |T| = Theta(m) in the R3 hard regime. (c) Delta-matroid placement, checked at the source (Eiben-Koana-Wahlstroem arXiv 2502.13654 / ESA 2026, Sec. 1.2): satisfiable <=> some U exactly a disjoint union of E_h is feasible in D(B) twisted by V. Theorem 6 (FPT k^O(k)) is Triangle Cover with F subset V(T') (partial triangles allowed); the exactly-partitioned variant is 3-Delta-matroid Parity, stated W[1]-hard there. Their linear delta-matroids are skew-symmetric with zero diagonal in char 2; our B has a diagonal (private variables). So the reduction lands on the W[1]-hard side; no algorithm follows. No obligation closed.

statement: RELATIONAL FACTORISATION - logical strength (director, 2026-11-26; no new lane, under CONV-D seq 17216). By the owner's constant-block counterexample (tool map row), for q = N^{beta+o(1)} blocks all local predicates can be trivial while the inter-block relation carries the whole Gap-MCSP hardness: on x(j,z) = g(j) the relation IS Gap-MCSP of the q-bit table g. A request for an 'efficient formula for the cross-block consistency relation of MCSP' is therefore a reformulation of the target, not a reduction. It becomes a genuine sub-obligation only together with a PROVEN structure of that relation (equality-type, low rank, bounded interface) that makes it cheaper than Gap-MCSP itself; none is known, and FOURIER-SUP seq 17183 and TRUNC2 seq 17202 (lossless, full-rank interfaces) point against a low-rank structure. The open point is thus: a non-product, non-enumerative formula for the shared-witness coupling (SEP-MERGE-LB excludes product forms, SEP-ELIM-LB excludes separator analyses independent of the hypothesis circuits).

statement: CONTROL THEOREM K AND STATUS AFTER THE OWNER CHECK OF THEOREM H (CLAIMED; cross-family mission iteration 14 submitted). (1) Owner algebraic check of Theorem H step 4 (17916): agrees with the PI exact kernel computation. Gadget rows give C_0 = C_1 = C_2; the triangle gives A + B + C = 0, hence A_0 = A_1 = A_2; line sums give multiples of J. Steps 5 and 6 give divisibility inside L_G, not only coordinatewise. No assumption on G beyond unpinned and 3-colourable. (2) Theorem K (owner): let S be a nonempty affine subspace of F3^n of codimension r. Then acn(F3^n minus S) = 2r. Proof checked by PI. Translate and quotient by the direction space of S to reach F3^r minus {0}. The cover x_i = 1, x_i = 2 gives <= 2r. For the lower bound, every covering subspace avoids 0, so it lies in an affine hyperplane l_i = 1 with l_i linear (choose l_i zero on the direction space and 1 at a base point). Then P = prod (1 - l_i) is the indicator of 0. Its reduced form is prod_j (1 - x_j^2) of degree 2r, and reduction does not raise degree, so k >= 2r. Literature: the hyperplane case is Alon-Fueredi 1993 (covering all but one point of a grid needs sum(|S_i| - 1) hyperplanes; here 2r). The extension from subspaces to hyperplanes is immediate. Related: Jamison 1977, Brouwer-Schrijver 1978 (blocking sets, k(q-1)+1). Alon-Fueredi and Brouwer-Schrijver were seen via search results; the Jamison citation is not verified at the source. K is therefore classical, not new. (3) Use: an exact per-stage optimum for the Gauss control. At stage t (eliminated set E) the projection of S = {Ax = b} has codimension rank A - rank A_E, so the optimum is 2(rank A - rank A_E), or 1 if S is empty. (4) Owner restriction of Fable's conclusion, accepted. 'Prism gives no extra simplification' is proved for the full pinned colouring set. For the positive representation, every projection creates only per-component shifts of G[T] (17915 R3). For the complement representation and arbitrary elimination orders it is not proved. The identification of existence elimination with dag-like resolution over linear equations mod 3 needs a formal simulation (F3-valued vs 0/1 variables); not done. (5) Status: prism lattice theorem algebraically checked by PI and owner; U_H with gadget variables is an exact identity; merging calculus is incomplete (17917); K is exact and classical. A proof of P != NP remains open. No obligation closed.

statement: OWNER DEEP RESEARCH 2026-11-19 (interface entropy -> P vs NP) with director source check: (a) no universal transfer from treewidth/separators/NOF to arbitrary algorithms; NOF -> ACC0 only (Hastad-Goldmann, Beigel-Tarui); P not in ACC0 does not give P != NC1. (b) Owner counterexample (exact): D_r = AND_{i<j} EXACT1(a,y_i,y_j) has treewidth r and is SAT (a=1, y=0); glued to F8 via a (GF(3) solution shifted so a=1, y=0) it is GF(3)-consistent, UNSAT, connected, of unbounded treewidth, with a constant-size core - large treewidth of a formula does not imply hardness (the family is refuted in poly time by bounded-width resolution). (c) Sources checked by the director on the web: ETH refutation claims by OpenAI and Anthropic (late Oct 2026, ~2^{n/(log n)^{1/2+o(1)}} for fixed-width k-SAT/#SAT) are widely reported (TechCrunch 2026-10-27, Fortnow blog) but independent verification is still in progress; Lean is reported for OpenAI, for Anthropic unconfirmed. Chukhin-Gajulapalli-Golovnev-Mihajlin (arXiv 2611.07972, ECCC TR26-313) confirmed: unconditional NE not in SIZE(2^n/(2n)) OR VP0_Z != VNP0_Z. Mishra-Santhanam 4n-O(log n) general-circuit bound: found only as a STOC 2027 submission claim (depends on Li s affine dispersers) - unverified. (d) Evaluation rule: algorithmic results also count through proved algorithm-to-lower-bound transfers (Williams; PIT), added to the research brief; a 2^{o(n)} k-SAT algorithm alone is no P-time algorithm and does not by itself give a new circuit lower bound (CNF lower bounds are already known).

statement: LEMMA W - status corrected (owner review 2026-11-19): it is the EASY direction of Hlineny-Whittle, 'Matroid tree-width', Theorem 3.2 (tree-width of a graph G with an edge equals the tree-width of its cycle matroid M(G)), restated for represented matroids: rows with supports as cliques of the coefficient graph instead of edges as cliques of G. Definition checked against the paper (final version, fi.muni.cz/~hlineny/papers/matr-tw-final.pdf, eq. (MW)): node width = sum_i r_M(E - F_i) - (d-1) r(M), exactly as used. The argument (map each element to a bag containing its support; ranks of the branch complements bounded by bag size) is the standard one; treat it as a straightforward / folklore generalisation, NOT as a new or 'proposed' result. The +1 (rank of a bag's coordinate vectors is <= |bag|, vs |bag| - 1 for a spanning forest of a graphic bag) is the only difference to the graphic case. A source stating the matrix version explicitly was not found in a short search (Cunningham-Geelen IPCO 2007 / ILP branch-width literature is the likely place).

statement: Dispute K11-D5, verified source step. MMW19 (STOC 2019) Thm 1.4, third bullet, read from the primary PDF (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, offset 13500, sha256 7077714b...): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on inputs of length N=2^n does not have circuits of N*poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP not in P/poly. CONSEQUENCES: (a) with A = empty oracle (in PH) and s(n)=n^c, a lower bound for DECISION MCSP[m^c] against general circuits of size N*(log N)^k (any depth) gives the search hypothesis, because a search solver's flag bit is a decision circuit of the same size and depth; (b) therefore no separate H2 premise is needed, and NP-in-P/poly-to-small-MCSP-circuits is carried by the theorem. OPEN: (i) the quantifier in Thm 1.4 ('for all n' vs 'infinitely many n') is not yet read; (ii) H1 itself, a general-circuit lower bound N*polylog(N) for decision MCSP[m^c], is unproved and is the real remaining obligation (see Q-f1e058b72f). The transfer relativizes (any oracle in PH). This is a magnification connection, not a LOWER_BOUND record.

R_G(X) = prod_{e={u,v}} sum_c M_{u,e,c} M_{v,e,c} with M_{v,e,c} = sum_{alpha: alpha(e)=c} X_{v,alpha}: on X_v = e_{j_v} the factor is [alpha_u(e) = alpha_v(e)], so R_G = H = Z on all unit-vector inputs; arithmetic circuit size O(d q^4) (d*deg*q sums of q^3 variables plus e*q products), deg R_G = 2e. statement: WITNESS GENERATOR from D-018 (owner 2026-11-19): adding a constant c to all coordinates keeps every clause sum mod 3 (3c = 0), and two distinct values can always be shifted onto {0,1}; a constant vector is never a solution. Hence every GF(3) solution of a BLIND formula uses all three values, and every blind formula on n variables is, up to isomorphism, a subset of the clauses allowed by a witness with value counts (k0,k1,k2), all >= 1, up to cyclic shift. n=7: 5 types, 2^10+2^10+2^12+2^13+2^11 = 16,384 candidate clause sets instead of 2^35. Upper bounds on candidates: n=6: 320, n=7: 16,384, n=8: 5,046,272, n=9: 12,519,997,440 (before dedup). Minimal-UNSAT reduction: every UNSAT formula contains an MUS; a GF(3)-inconsistent MUS has no integer solution and is refuted by one CG round (D-023); adding clauses only shrinks the first CG closure - so the maximal CG rank over all UNSAT formulas on <= n variables is attained on blind MUS classes.

statement: DIRECTOR NOTE on HYPOTHESIS seq 4825 (R0400, model nemotron3-nano-30b): "positive 1-in-3 SAT over GF(3) admits an exact GF(3)-Nullstellensatz certificate of degree 3, size O(n^2), constructed and verified in polynomial time". (1) Its cited evidence does not exist: dataset agent_agent_topic_onein3_gap_v1_da4f93e6 (9 KB, columns n,m,first,subsets,cons,sat,gap,sat_nocons) has no columns gf3_nullstellensatz_degree/_size; no dataset has them. (2) It generalises n <= 7 to all n. (3) It conflicts with established results: a certificate of bounded degree d for every UNSAT formula would be found in n^O(d) time (Clegg-Edmonds-Impagliazzo), i.e. P = NP; Omega(n) PC degree lower bounds for 3-colouring hold over every field (Lauria-Nordstrom 2017) and transfer to positive 1-in-3 (claim:efc141766fe0, KNOWN). statement: STAGE A SOURCE CHECK, row B, closed against the primary PDF (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, sha256 7077714b...). Thm 1.4 (verbatim): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if there is eps>0 such that for all c>=1, search-MCSP^A[2^{eps n/c}] on inputs of length N=2^n has no N^{1+eps}-size O(1/eps)-depth TC0 circuits, then NP is not in TC0. The same paper's Thm 1.3 hypothesis is a super-linear-time worst-case lower bound for search-MCSP against deterministic streaming algorithms with sub-linear space. Row B's earlier citation (a circuit-to-formula route via Thm 1.4) is WRONG: Thm 1.4 is a TC0 result for the search version with an oracle A in PH. The text also confirms that OPS18 uses an O(n)-approximation MCSP[2^{eps n}] with N^{1+delta}-size circuits to get NP not in P/poly, consistent with row A.

statement: PI CHECK OF THE 2026-11-27 OWNER SYNTHESIS (elimination identities, lattices, Kempe, prism; CLAIMED, Claude family; Fable's review is also Claude family, so no cross-family review yet). (1) Elimination identities: correct. Q(t,u) = R(u) prod_{j<=d} (t - r_j(u))^2. For d <= 2, exists t with Q = 1 iff R = 1. For d = 3, three elements of F3 are pairwise distinct iff r1+r2+r3 = 0 and r1 != r2. If r1+r2+r3 = 0 and r1 != r2, then r3 = r1 would give r2 = -2r1 = r1. These are the 3-factor case of the closure lemma 17910: the bad set {sum = 0, r1 - r2 = 1} union {sum = 0, r1 - r2 = 2} consists of two codim-2 subspaces instead of six codim-3 points. (2) Union rule: U cup (v+U) cup (2v+U) = U + <v> over F3. Implemented as coset merging {Ax in b + <d>} = {CAx = Cb} with ker C = <d>, to a fixpoint, then pruning (scratchpad/aelim/merge.py). 0/150 mismatches against brute force. Peaks on random 3-colouring at m = 2.3n, n = 8..16, 3 seeds: 17-47 subspaces with merging against 27-115 without, about 2.2-2.9n. Small sizes only; no asymptotic claim. (3) Satz A, arbitrary order (owner strengthening): proof correct. Project to r coordinates injective on the Q-span; generators have entries in {-1,0,1}, so norm <= sqrt r. A rank step multiplies the covolume by at most sqrt r, a same-rank strict extension divides it by at least 2, and the final covolume is >= 1. So k <= (r/2) log2 r, and Fable's two-phase restriction is unnecessary. (4) Satz B, 3L <= M <= L: correct for unpinned graphs only. Fable's pinned counterexample is accepted: pinned prism, ranks 3 and 2 over Q. (5) Lemma F, general form: correct. If S is closed under global colour permutations, x + rho x + rho^2 x = 1 and q is invariant, then an affine q = Bx + b is constant on S in char != 3. (6) Universal prism transformation H(G), |V| = 7n+3, a_v = bottom vertex opposite R0 of prism A_v, b_v = bottom vertex opposite R1 of prism B_v, triangle v a_v b_v. (a) Each colour of v has exactly one extension (table checked by hand), so Col3(H) = 6 |Col3(G)|. (b) PI proof that each colour pair {c,c'} induces a connected subgraph in every colouring. A prism bottom vertex p_i of colour c is adjacent to R_{c'} if i = c'. Otherwise i is the third colour, and its bottom neighbour of colour c' sits at index c, hence is adjacent to R_c. Every original v of colour c has a neighbour in {a_v, b_v} of colour c'. So Kempe swaps are global transpositions and #Kempe classes = |Col3(G)|. (c) [L_H : M_H] = 3^r with r = rank_Q of the one-hot colouring differences of G: verified exactly (integer HNF) on 15 graphs, among them K3, C5, C6 and G = prism, where rank_F3 = 7 < rank_Q = 8 and the index is still 3^8. Upper bound proved: L/M is generated by the image of W ~ L_G (rank r) and killed by 3. Lower bound open: the prism readouts epsilon give only 3^{rank_F3}, which is insufficient for G = prism. The owner's tensor argument L/M ~ W (x) (T/J) has unproved steps (injectivity, the separate summand). So (c) is computational evidence plus a proved upper bound, not a theorem. (7) Relevance: the index is 3^{2n} already for edgeless G, so it carries no hardness. (8) First unproved statement of the strongest chain (Phase 3 of the owner plan): a property that polynomial-time selection S must have and that contradicts a proved theorem. None has been derived. Every consequence derived so far (selection, lattice generators, tropical value, elimination) relativizes (cf. 17590) or also holds for exponential-time algorithms. No obligation closed.

statement: DEGREE-2 MEMBERSHIP (owner 2026-11-27, PI completed the proof; CLAIMED, Claude family). deg(p) = 2, neighbours u, v: e_p in W_G <=> some 3-colouring has col(u) = col(v), i.e. G/(u=v) is 3-colourable. (=>-contrapositive) If col(u) != col(v) always, then {col p, col u, col v} = {1,2,3} always and phi(z) = z_p + z_u + z_v vanishes on every Kempe vector: for a pair containing col p the partner neighbour is adjacent to p, so both lie in K with opposite signs; for the pair {col u, col v}, u and v must lie in the same component, since otherwise that swap would give col(u) = col(v), and then their signs cancel. phi(e_p) = 1. (<=) p is a singleton bichromatic component. Hand example with u, v non-adjacent but forced different checked. So unit-vector membership is 3-colourability after identifying two vertices: the Kempe space gives no independent mechanism for a lower bound (owner's conclusion).

Our non-equidimensionality result is for the SQUARE critical locus Sigma(perm_5)=Crit(perm_5) (5x5 matrix, 25 vars, all 4x4 sub-permanents=0) - a DIFFERENT variety (different ambient dim 25 vs 20, different equations 25 vs 5). statement: FruitStack-coordinated structural finding (2 PlumMe models + adversarial researcher). The models suggested the Young-flattening/catalecticant lever (Landsberg-Manivel) to avoid weight-space enumeration. I TESTED it directly and rigorously: the (2,2)-catalecticant rank (= dim span second partials) is 36 for det_4 (= C(4,2)^2, apolarity-GENERIC) but only 18 for z*perm_3; gradient rank 16 vs 10. So the catalecticant SEPARATES, but in the REVERSE direction: z*perm_3 has LOW apolarity rank because it is a REDUCIBLE product z*perm_3 (degenerate), while det_4 is apolarity-generic (high rank). Hence the (r+1)-minors of the catalecticant vanish on z*perm_3 but NOT on det_4 - an equation of the PERMANENT closure violated by the determinant (reverse/trivial direction, consistent with the (4,4,4,4,4) d=5 finding). CONCLUSION: apolarity/catalecticant/low-rank conditions ALL go the wrong way for perm-vs-det, because the determinant is apolarity-generic, not low-rank. The FORWARD separating property (perm not in det closure) cannot be a low-rank condition; it must use the determinant's SPECIAL geometry: its DEGENERATE DUAL variety (dual of {det_n=0} = Segre of rank-1 matrices, projective dim 2n-1 << n^2-2). This is exactly the Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre 'hypersurfaces with degenerate duals and the GCT program' lever - a forward-separating condition. (Both models NOT_VERIFIED and conflicting on specifics - degree 6 vs 36 vs a claimed degree-5 ABV separating equation that CONTRADICTS my verified d=5 no-separation result; adversarial web researcher is verifying the real LMR/Alper-Bogart-Velasco results.)

statement: ELIMINATION-DEGREE in the Boolean quotient ring (owner 2026-11-27), CLAIMED, author-checked (Claude family), exhaustive check and_chain_check.py. (1) Joint pivot over F_2: exists t with a_i t + b_i = 0 for all i <=> (1+a_i)b_i = 0 and a_i b_j + a_j b_i = 0 (all i,j); one step raises degree to <= 3 from quadratic. Over F_3 with Boolean t the formula is false (8 counterexamples for m=2, e.g. a=(0,1), b=(0,2)). (2) Any system in visible variables only describing d = x_1...x_n needs an equation of degree >= n (restrict d=0; multilinear representation unique, indicator of 1^n is prod x_i); d - prod x_i attains n; holds over every field. (3) Positive exact-one AND gate E(t,u,~a), E(t,v,~b), E(u,v,s) forces t = ab (s = XNOR, third clause forces uv=0); complements via E(x,~x,z); zero without repeated literals: E(x,y,z), E(x,y,w), E(z,w,r) forces z=w=0. Chain checked n<=6: projection = graph of AND_n, aux unique. O(n) clauses, bounded treewidth (path decomposition per gate plus z; width not computed). Consequence: degree after elimination is unbounded already at bounded treewidth, while the factored (aux/extension) form has width 2. The fitting measure is width/rank of the factored representation, for which 17405 (CLAIMED) gives 2^p for P_B; degree lower bounds (BGIP 2001) are for PC without extension variables. Not in proofbook before (closest: ACC0-L3 class D, row 4864, NAND gadget over GF(3)). No obligation closed, no runtime bound.

statement: SCOPE CHECK of the law cov = rank3 + 1 on GF(3)-blind positive 1-in-3 families (director 2026-11-21, owner request): FALSE in general. Exact counterexamples: core F0 = {012,013,045,145,234,235} is blind with cov 6, rank3 5 (difference 1), but F0 + {678} is blind with cov 9, rank3 6 (difference 3) and F0 + a disjoint shifted copy is blind with cov 12, rank3 10 (difference 2) - for variable-disjoint families cov and rank add, consistency and unsatisfiability are kept. This refutes the general claims claim:adb072e397b9 and claim:b74d679e26ba as stated. PROVED (elementary): a minimally blind family (blind, no proper subfamily blind) is connected; and minimality needs only the subfamilies with one clause removed. NOT proved: minimally blind => cov = rank3 + 1. Finite evidence (exhaustive, all families on <= 6 variables with m <= 8 clauses): all 900 minimally blind families have m = 5 and cov - rank3 = 1, no counterexample. The dataset laws on n = 7, m = 6 and n = 8 hold there by the size constraint (two disjoint blind cores need more variables), which explains the observation without supporting the general law. Owner decision: no further four-agent campaign on this law until the minimal-core version is proved or refuted.

statement: REFRAMING of M_5 via Xie + the tangent-space bound. rank Hess(perm_5)(X) = 25 - dim T_X Sigma (Zariski tangent space to Crit(perm_5)=V(I_4(5,5))), <= 25 - dim_X Sigma (LOCAL dim). Our data give TWO components: (i) the n-2=3-row-supported '2-zero-rows' family, dim = n(n-2)=15 (Xie's maximal component), Hessian rank 10; (ii) the block family diag(B,C), dim 11, Hessian rank 14. So Sigma(perm_5) is NOT equidimensional. M_5 = 25 - d_min where d_min = minimal tangent-space dim over singular points. Xie gives the MAXIMAL dim (15) -> rank 10 there, which does NOT bound M_5 from above. M_5=14 IFF no component of Sigma(perm_5) has dim <= 10 (at a point with reduced/<=10-dim tangent space). Xie does NOT settle this (gives max, not min, dim; reducedness of I_4(5,5) open).

statement: BEYOND PC (owner deep research 2026-11-19, director checks): (1) IPS TRANSFER SCHEMA: in GF(2)[x,y] (no multilinearisation) the substitution y -> 1+a+b maps L_edge to 0, q_edge to ab + (a^2+a) + (b^2+b), y^2+y to (a^2+a)+(b^2+b) (sympy-checked); vertex axioms map to colouring axioms. Substituting a 3-term affine form into an ARITHMETIC CIRCUIT costs only additive size, so a size-s circuit-coefficient IPS refutation of F(G) gives a size-O(s+|G|) IPS refutation of the 3-colouring axioms of G (formal size statement still to be fixed). Unlike roABP-IPS (order-sensitive), general IPS has no width obstacle here. (2) Grochow-Pitassi 2014: any superpolynomial IPS lower bound implies VP != VNP - so an IPS lower bound for F(G) is at least as hard as VP != VNP; the transfer shows F(G) is no easier than 3-colouring, it does not provide the bound. (3) Hardness magnification (Oliveira-Pich-Santhanam): slightly superlinear bounds for Gap-MCSP would give NP not in P/poly; director note: magnification is limited by the LOCALITY BARRIER (Chen-Hirahara-Oliveira-Pich-Rajgopal-Santhanam 2020) - known lower-bound techniques extend to oracle-augmented circuits and cannot supply the needed bounds. No direct link from our 1-in-3 results. (4) Quantifier gap stays explicit: hard instances for a proof system say nothing about every circuit computing SAT_N. (5) Mishra-Santhanam 4n - O(log n): still only verified by the director as a STOC 2027 submission claim.

statement: T11-O (honest rigorous bracket, no false shortcut): the minimal forward-separation degree for perm_3 vs det_4 satisfies 6 <= d_min^sep(3,4) <= 24. LOWER BOUND 6: verified (I(D_4)_5={0} via rectangular null-cone T11-N + 23 five-row d=5 certificates + BHIM symmetroid bound for ell<=4; separation excluded at d<=5). UPPER BOUND 24: the Landsberg-Manivel-Ressayre degenerate-dual module (degree 2n(n-1)=24 for det_4) is a genuine separator - it is exactly the representation-theoretic form of the Mignon-Ressayre quadratic bound dc(perm_m)>=m^2/2, which for m=3 gives dc(perm_3)>=5>4, i.e. perm_3 NOT in closure(det_4); so a separator exists at degree 24. The clean/known separator sits exactly at the quadratic (T8 Hessian) degree 24. HONEST META: we have NOT reduced the perm-vs-det question; we have rigorously bracketed the smallest-degree geometric separator for this one small case and tied its upper end to the quadratic barrier, without inventing a shortcut that contradicts our own exact certificates.

statement: ORACLE ELIMINATION COUNT DOES NOT BEAR ON ALGEBRIZATION; PI CORRECTION (owner 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family; AW from memory). Owner's (a) no p(m)-bit oracle-free graph represents every A:{0,1}^m->{0,1} (2^{2^m} > 2^{p(m)+1}) and (b) a query compiler needs B >= 2^m answer bits: both correct, and both are the Shannon counting argument. They hold for every oracle, algebraic or not, so they cannot separate algebrizing from non-algebrizing proofs. No relativized or algebrized proof eliminates the oracle; the standard relativized form keeps oracle gates as external oracle constraints (relativized Cook-Levin), and the algebrization test asks whether each step stays valid with Ã-constraints on the C side and A on the D side. Explicit local decomposition (local checkability, Arora-Impagliazzo-Vazirani) is exactly what arithmetization uses, and AW show arithmetization-based results such as IP=PSPACE algebrize. PI correction to the 2026-11-27 chat proposal: 'all tools algebrize => no combination proves P!=NP' is too strong. AW algebrization is asymmetric (Ã vs A) and not closed under composition of inclusions, so a tool-level check is necessary but not sufficient. The whole proof must be tested. No obligation closed.

structure.text: SOURCE CHECK row G (Stage A, lane T-B). Source read: arXiv 2312.08163v1, Pich-Santhanam, 'Towards P != NP from Extended Frege lower bounds' (the longer version of ECCC TR23-199; the ECCC PDF was NOT read). Read via web_read at offset 0 and 4500. Theorem 1 (extraction, verbatim wording as far as the text goes): let k>=1 be constant. (1) If there is a p-time f such that for each big n, wk_n(f) is a tautology, and EF + wk(f) is not p-bounded, then SAT_n is not in Circuit[n^{eps k}] for infinitely many n. (2) If there is a p-time f with S12 proving W^k_{n0}(f) for some n0, and EF is not p-bounded, the same conclusion holds. eps>0 is universal. Corollary 1 (partial extraction): if for every k there is a p-time f_k with wk_n(f_k) tautologies for big n, and EF + wk(f_k) is not p-bounded for each k, then NP is not in SIZE[n^l] for every l, i.e. SAT is not in P/poly. Scope and status: row G's conclusion (SAT not in P/poly) needs (i) witnessing functions f_k for EVERY k and (ii) the superpolynomial proof-size lower bound for EF + wk(f_k). The paper says it does NOT know an unconditional witnessing function (it is the step it cannot yet discharge). Row G is therefore VERIFIED AS A CONDITIONAL STATEMENT; both (i) and (ii) remain open. The abstract's separate P != NP route (conditions I-II, S12 witnessing) is not the row-G route and is not checked here.

statement: SCOPE CHECK of the owner/ChatGPT 'own formula as centre' note (2026-11-27, director; CLAIMED). (1) Affine characterisation (MS-0.25 Thm 1, seq 10965; 0/1 form seq 3982): F_E satisfiable iff the F_3 affine space A_E z = 1 contains a 0/1 point. Two-line proof (three bits summing to 1 mod 3 sum to 1). Exact, but an elementary reformulation; no hardness transfer. (2) w*(F(G)) = 2 tw(G) + 1 (Lean, seq 4079/8730): scope = the 3-colouring exact-one family F(G) only, minimum over spanning families of the F_3 kernel, measure = treewidth of the coefficient graph. Not about nonlinear reparametrisations, other encodings or other algorithms. Open: definition-fidelity review and novelty check (Q-5f55fb62c2). (3) Product identity: over F_3, (t-2)^2 = 1 for t in {0,1} and 0 for t = 2, so P_B(y) = prod_i (x_0 + B y)_i - 2)^2 is the indicator of 0/1 points of x_0 + B F_3^d. Correct. Equivalently: F_E satisfiable iff the N affine hyperplanes {y : (x_0 + B y)_i = 2} do NOT cover F_3^d (a reformulation; hyperplane covering is coNP-complete in general). For E = F(G) the primal graph of the factors of P_B is the coefficient graph of B, so min_B tw(primal) = 2 tw(G) + 1 holds directly. Consequence, exact strength: variable elimination over ANY linear kernel parametrisation costs >= 3^{2 tw(G) + 2} = 9^{tw(G)+1} (unconditional, for this algorithm class only), while the standard colouring DP on G costs 3^{tw(G)} poly. So w* measures the cost of the linear representation, not intrinsic hardness; P_B always has small circuits (product of N squared affine forms), so no algebraic lower bound for P_B follows. No proof progress; no new lane.

statement: Dispute K11-D5, resolved on the H2 point by source. MMW19 (STOC 2019) Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (primary PDF, offset 13500; proof at offset 53500, sha256 7077714b...): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on N=2^n inputs has no circuits of size N*poly(s(n)) and depth poly(s(n)), then NP not in P/poly. The proof is a contrapositive: NP in P/poly collapses PH to P/poly, and the Lemma 3.1 construction is uniform in n, so it yields small circuits at every input length. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the NP-to-small-MCSP conversion (the former H2) is inside the theorem, not an extra premise; (2) the quantifier is therefore 'infinitely many n' (inferred from the proof structure, not verbatim text); (3) with A empty and s(n)=n^c, a general-circuit lower bound N*(log N)^k for every fixed k, infinitely often, for decision MCSP[m^c] gives the search hypothesis, because a decision circuit of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s) yields a search circuit of the same size and depth (flag bit; the flag-bit cost itself is not checked here). OPEN: H1 itself (a general-circuit decision lower bound for MCSP[m^c] at N*(log N)^k, infinitely often) is unproved and is the only remaining obligation; see Q-10bbdfaf2a and Q-f1e058b72f. This is a magnification connection, not a LOWER_BOUND record, and not a lemma.

statement: The universal form of the law sat = cons3 over all positive 1-in-3 formulas is equivalent to P = NP: cons3 is decidable in polynomial time by Gaussian elimination over GF(3), and 1-in-3-SAT is NP-complete. So the exact-law question on this family is a restatement of P vs NP, not a route around it. Finite data can only locate the boundary of the law; the boundary currently sits in the random n=10-12 and targeted rank-7-9 families.

statement: The Oliveira-Pich-Santhanam ToC 2021 Theorem 1.4 (near-quadratic formula bound) states: there exists an explicit function f in E^NP such that any fan-in-2 formula computing f has size N^{2-o(1)}. Combined with the circuit-to-formula unfolding: circuit depth d => formula size ≤2^{d+1}-1. Setting 2^{d+1}-1 ≥ N^{2-ε} gives d ≥ (2-ε)log₂N - 1. This links the lower bound to circuit depth, not general size.

statement: SOURCE CHECK, MMW19 (STOC 2019, primary PDF, people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf). Verbatim quantifiers: (Thm 1.2) for s(n) >= n time-constructible and any oracle A, one-pass streaming for search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs runs in 2^n * O~(s) time, O~(s^2) worst-case update time, O~(s) space, using a Sigma3SAT^A oracle with queries of length O~(s). Algorithm 1 consumes t = 100 s log s bits per block; its update-time analysis (Sec. 4 proof) gives O~(t^2) per block, consistent with Thm 1.2. (Thm 1.3) If there is A in PH such that search-MCSP^A[s] has no poly(s)-space streaming algorithm with poly(s) update time, then P != NP. Proof (Sec. 5, read at offset 49500): contrapositive; under P = NP, PH collapses, Sigma3SAT^A is in P for every A in PH, each Circuit-Min-Merge query of length O(s log s) is replaced by a poly(s)-time computation, giving poly(s) update time. (Thm 1.4 and 1.5 read at offsets 54000 and 58500; statements as in the bridge map.) Scope: this is a source verification of statements and proof structure only. It does not verify the 2^n*s total-time accounting beyond cm-b098520d49db4fa4, and it does not establish any lower bound. The lower bound needed for P != NP is an update-time lower bound (space and communication alone cannot reach it, per the owner's note), and none is proved here.

statement: FOUR-DIMENSION PROFILE (owner 2026-11-19, replaces the 'common axis'): every representation sigma(F) of a formula is judged on (1) EXACTNESS - is the decision information present; (2) SIZE - worst-case size; (3) CONSTRUCTION - cost to build it from F (and to update it clause by clause); (4) EVALUATION - cost to extract SAT from it. Two different failure kinds: INFORMATION LOSS (a summary like [V_F != empty] maps a satisfiable and a GF(3)-blind UNSAT formula to the same value - 1,350 blind sets at n=6) versus HARD EXTRACTION: the full affine GF(3) solution space V_F = {x in F_3^n : A x = 1} is built by Gaussian elimination in polynomial time and is EXACT, since a clause sum over {0,1} is in 0..3 and only 1 is 1 mod 3, so V_F intersect {0,1}^n = the Boolean solutions; deciding whether an affine subspace of F_3^n contains a 0/1 point is therefore NP-complete. Indistinguishability pairs can never refute an exact representation; for those the open question is the evaluation cost. P = NP needs all four dimensions polynomial for every F; a limit of one representation or one evaluation method is not P != NP. Measured Nullstellensatz degrees on finite instances (local degree 4 at k=17) are data, not an asymptotic growth claim; n^O(d) is an upper bound for degree-d search only.

label: 25e7d18f638c527c
statement: VERIFIED ALGEBRAIC TRANSFER, steps 4-6 (owner contract 2026-11-27; PI reading of both papers; CLAIMED, Claude family). EXTERNAL INPUTS, UNVERIFIED, kept separate from Proofbook results: OpenAI 'VP and VNP are different' (openai/math 3344da5, Lean OAI.Computability.VPVNP.Standalone.vp_ne_vnp) and Anthropic 'VP != VNP over every field' (anthropics/formal-math 11b6c7e, vp-vnp, Lean Solution.mainTheorem etc.). Kernel build, #print axioms and Comparator are running in a bwrap sandbox; results follow in a separate row. STEP 4, mechanism. Both proofs trade tensor rigidity against diagonalization. Anthropic: Thm 2.2 (thm_alt) gives a flat or a contracting case. Flat case: lem_balanced splits the polynomial at every gate, so the output coefficient tensor is a sum of terms of rank <= L across balanced sets; Euclidean prices force log L >= l k^{3/2}/16 for f_{k,l}. Contracting case: thm_cut, with no circuit, cuts every weighted nondeterministic computation into short pieces; lem_lowdeg turns a circuit of size v^a into an accelerator, a program whose circuit constants act only as multiplicative named weights and whose runs take v^{H-16} < v^H steps; lem_postpone and prop_next amplify; thm_noacc gives V = 1 + V, impossible. OpenAI: Euclidean tensor pricing (exists_balanced_cutFactors, see 17563) plus replay diagonalization against the counting family f_n, whose c_x counts accepting paths of a universal machine. In both proofs the circuit enters only at the C-steps (formal multilinear block part or formal low-degree part); the hard families enter only through clause sums. STEP 5, translation. By 17584 over the semiring F[Y] with weights set to variables, every clause sum is a p-projection of U_G for a polynomial-size pinned graph G: boolean vertices carry the bits, AND gadgets give indicator vertices for local assignments, and their colour-1 variables are replaced by the local weights. f_{k,l}, Phi and f_n are clause sums, so each is a projection of a U_G family. This is a corollary of 17584 and not new; Valiant/Buergisser parsimonious completeness is standard (from memory). Consequence, conditional on the external results: the U_G families are not in VP. That is a consequence, not a premise. STEP 6, P = NP against intermediate theorems; result negative and exact. (a) C-steps. A polynomial-time SAT algorithm yields Boolean circuits, that is F2-circuits for some g = f + sum_i (x_i^2 - x_i) h_i. lem_balanced and lem_lowdeg read the multilinear block part and the low-degree part of the formal output, and for such g these are unrelated to f. Counterexamples: Anthropic Sec. 2.5, where (x11^2 - x11) x21...xk1 vanishes on {0,1} but has nonzero block-linear part; 17571, IP_n with a linear-size circuit and full cut rank. So the hypotheses of the C-steps are not met. (b) Diagonal step. thm_noacc refutes accelerators. A uniform algorithm from P = NP, or even from P^#P = P, is an accelerator only if it computes the weighted sum of tau-plain instances, size v^{H-32}, in v^{H-16} steps. Collapse simulations raise the time exponent by the factor c of the assumed algorithm and never lower it below the plain-run bound, so no accelerator arises. A nonuniform Boolean circuit branches on its advice; that is excluded by the model, because names may only be multiplied in (Anthropic 2.5: 'no way to run it faster than gate by gate'). Hence no intermediate theorem of either proof is contradicted by P = NP along these derivations. The exact obstruction: formal polynomial structure (C-steps) and exponent-lowering speedup in the weighted-sum model (diagonal step). No new lower-bound premise and no conditional chain; no obligation closed.

statement: PB VIEW OF THE BLIND CASES - synthesis of findings already on file (owner 2026-11-19 PB question): the PB encoding x_i+x_j+x_k = 1, x in {0,1} is exact, but exactness is not cheap inference. (1) The LP relaxation is NEVER infeasible: x = 1/3 everywhere satisfies every clause (D-016h), so pure linear arithmetic over [0,1] refutes no positive 1-in-3 formula. (2) Depth-1 Chvatal-Gomory from A x = 1 alone refutes exactly the integer-infeasible formulas (D-023, integer Farkas / Hermite normal form). (3) Of the 1,350 GF(3)-blind sets at n=6 only 30 are integer-infeasible (R0100/R0101). So the cheap PB steps catch 30 of 1,350; the other 1,320 need the bounds 0 <= x <= 1 combined with deeper cuts or conflict learning - that is where the PB information difference sits.

statement: BRIDGE STATUS (owner 2026-11-19, literature-checked): (1) A computation trace is NOT an UNSAT proof by itself (an always-UNSAT program has short checkable traces); it becomes one only together with a proof of the algorithm s correctness. Precise known form: if the correctness of a poly-time algorithm A is provable in the bounded arithmetic PV (S^1_2), then A s UNSAT answers translate into polynomial-size Extended Frege proofs (Cook 1975; Krajicek-Pudlak). An EF lower bound would therefore exclude all poly-time algorithms with PV-provable correctness, not all algorithms. (2) Cook-Reckhow: NP = coNP iff some propositional proof system is polynomially bounded; superpolynomial lower bounds for EVERY proof system give NP != coNP (hence P != NP); a lower bound for one system (PC, EF) does not, since existence of a p-optimal proof system is open. (3) Alekseev, A lower bound for polynomial calculus with extension rule (CCC 2021 version; owner cites 2026 journal version): exponential BIT-SIZE lower bound over Q for the Binary Value Principle 1 + x1 + 2x2 + ... + 2^(n-1)xn = 0 in PC with extension variables (and radical-type rules) - bit-level/coefficient size as the measured resource, not a CNF and not over GF(2). For ALG-BIT-001 (no new assignment): report the coefficient BIT SIZE of certificates alongside degree when working over Q/Z (e.g. integer-sum refutations of blind cores, which relate to the CG certificates).
